items.title: Small Models Have Arrived
items.summary: The fast/cheap/good-enough models have quietly gotten good. That unlocks consumer AI, and most of the "token spewer" work that actually runs a business.

items.title: Durable Objects are Made for Agents
items.summary: I've spent the last few months building almost exclusively on Cloudflare Durable Objects. They're a near-perfect primitive for building agents—here's where they shine, and where they fall short.

items.title: The Oracle and the Firm
items.summary: Comparing two very different approaches to scaling context between Fable 5 and GPT 5.5.

items.title: Coding Agents in Feb 2026
items.summary: My point-in-time snapshot of using Claude Code and Codex together. Opus shines at context management and tool use, Codex writes fewer bugs. Here's how I use both.

items.title: How I Use Obsidian
items.summary: Obsidian has become my personal operating system for thinking and writing. Here's the golden rule I follow and the systems I use.

items.title: You Still Need to Think
items.summary: When it comes to coding agents, the product shape fundamentally shifts how you think.

items.title: The Coding Agent Metagame
items.summary: Using Claude Code feels more like playing the piano than shuffling tickets in Jira. I get the vague sense that by using the tool differently, I could become a virtuoso. Here's my best attempt to explain why that is.

items.title: Reflections on OpenAI
items.summary: There's a lot of smoke and noise around what OpenAI is doing, but not a lot of first-hand accounts of what the culture of working there actually feels like. Here's my view on what it was like to work there.

items.title: Upsides and Downsides
items.summary: When to shift mentality from upsides to downsides. And why most AI demos don't make great products.

items.title: How much of a manager are you?
items.summary: There's a lot of debate around how much 'good code' LLMs can write for you. Some engineers claim coding with LLMs is amazing, while others think they are trash. Ultimately, it depends on how much of a manager you are.
